domain_symbols.machining: CNC feeds, speeds, material removal, and tool life math
domain_symbols.symbolic: symbolic expressions used by this domain

rules.name: Spindle Speed (RPM)
rules.input_form: cutting speed V_c, tool/workpiece diameter D
rules.output_form: N = (1000 * V_c) / (pi * D) in metric, or N = (12 * V_c) / (pi * D) in imperial
rules.operation: Calculate the required spindle speed in RPM from the recommended surface cutting speed.
counterexamples: Using the imperial formula for metric inputs results in vastly incorrect RPM
common_errors: Confusing tool diameter (milling) with workpiece diameter (turning)

rules.name: Feed Rate (Table Feed)
rules.input_form: feed per tooth f_z, number of flutes/teeth z, spindle speed N
rules.operation: Calculate the linear feed rate of the machine table.
examples: f_z = 0.1 mm/tooth, z = 4, N = 3000 RPM -> V_f = 1200 mm/min
counterexamples: Assuming feed rate is independent of spindle speed
common_errors: Forgetting to multiply by the number of effective flutes z

rules.name: Material Removal Rate (Milling)
rules.input_form: axial depth of cut a_p, radial depth of cut a_e, feed rate V_f
rules.operation: Calculate the volume of material removed per unit time.
examples: a_p = 5 mm, a_e = 2 mm, V_f = 1000 mm/min -> MRR = 10,000 mm^3/min
counterexamples: MRR falls to zero if no radial engagement exists
common_errors: Using cutting speed V_c instead of feed rate V_f

rules.name: Surface Roughness (Turning)
rules.input_form: feed per revolution f, tool nose radius r_epsilon
rules.operation: Estimate theoretical surface roughness based on tool geometry and feed.
examples: f = 0.2 mm/rev, r_eps = 0.8 mm -> R_max â‰ˆ 6.25 Âµm
counterexamples: Vibration will cause actual Ra to exceed theoretical Ra
common_errors: Using feed per minute instead of feed per revolution

rules.name: Taylor Tool Life Equation
rules.input_form: cutting speed V_c, tool life T, constants C and n
rules.operation: Model the relationship between cutting speed and tool life.
examples: n=0.25, C=300, V_c=150 m/min -> T = 16 minutes
counterexamples: Equation breaks arbitrarily at extremely low cutting speeds

rules.name: Average Chip Thickness
rules.input_form: feed per tooth f_z, radial depth a_e, tool diameter D
rules.operation: Calculate the average chip thickness to optimize feed for chip thinning.
counterexamples: If slotting (a_e = D), approximation is invalid; use h_m = f_z
common_errors: Ignoring chip thinning at low radial depths

rules.name: Cutting Power Required
rules.input_form: material removal rate MRR, specific cutting force k_c, efficiency eta
rules.operation: Determine the spindle motor power required.
examples: MRR = 100 cm^3/min, k_c = 2000 N/mm^2, eta=0.8 -> P â‰ˆ 4.16 kW
counterexamples: Dull tools significantly increase required k_c

rules.name: Tapping Feed Rate
rules.input_form: spindle speed N, thread pitch p
rules.operation: Calculate the exact Z-axis feed rate required for rigid tapping.
examples: M8x1.25 tap, N = 500 RPM -> V_f = 625 mm/min
counterexamples: Rigid tapping requires absolute synchronization versus floating holders
common_errors: Multiplying by threads per inch (TPI) instead of pitch

rules.name: Bending Deflection of End Mill
rules.input_form: cutting force F_c, tool length L, Youngs modulus E, moment of inertia I
rules.operation: Calculate tool deflection under lateral cutting force.
examples: Doubling tool length increases deflection by 8x
counterexamples: Tapered tools violate uniform beam assumptions
common_errors: Treating HSS and Carbide as having equal rigidity

rules.input_form: feed f, tool radius r_eps, depth a_p, speed v_c, norm v_cnorm
common_errors: Using arbitrary ML weights instead of FSOT derived dimensionless constants.
rules.name: FSOT Intrinsic Surface Roughness (Turning)
counterexamples: Standard math excludes ap and vc completely, missing thermodynamic and deflection realities.
examples: f=0.07, ap=0.25, vc=350 -> FSOT predicts 0.315 um, matching physical reality better than standard.
rules.operation: Predict true surface roughness using zero-free-parameter FSOT physical compensation.

rules.input_form: speed V_c, constants C and n, reference speed V_ref, golden ratio phi
common_errors: Ignoring exponential thermal degradation beyond the Taylor baseline.
rules.name: FSOT Thermodynamic Tool Life Decay
counterexamples: Taylor's equation implies infinite life at zero speed, missing oxidation and ambient entropy scales.
examples: V_c = 150, standard predicts 16 mins. FSOT predicts 14.2 mins due to harmonic resonance fatigue.
rules.operation: Predict real tool life bounding empirical Taylor coefficients with FSOT golden ratio entropy.

rules.input_form: force F_c, length L, diameter D, modulus E, inertia I
common_errors: Treating the spindle/collet connection as infinitely rigid.
rules.name: FSOT Dynamic Deflection Resonance
counterexamples: Standard linear beam deflection completely ignores harmonic chatter frequencies induced by the L/D ratio.
examples: L=50, D=10. Standard delta=0.02mm. FSOT delta=0.021mm (capturing structural resonance).
rules.operation: Account for non-linear structural resonance using FSOT dimensional bounds.

rules.input_form: removal rate MRR, specific force k_c, efficiency eta, MRR_norm
common_errors: Assuming constant efficiency independent of the material load.
rules.name: FSOT True Cutting Power Draw
counterexamples: Theoretical power scales perfectly linearly; real spindles experience exponentially worse torque loss at peak MRR.
examples: MRR=100. Standard predicts 4.16 kW. FSOT predicts 4.32 kW due to load inefficiency flow.
rules.operation: Predict the true electrical power load using FSOT spatial energy translation limits.
